# Browsa

> A free, open source (MIT) web browser for Mac, written in Swift on WebKit, with Arc's way of working: a sidebar,
> Spaces, Favourites, pinned tabs, Split View, Glance, Boosts and Arc's keyboard shortcuts. Current release: 1.3
> (25 November 2026), for macOS 26 or later.

For a feature-by-feature account of the released Mac app, with the version each feature arrived in and the source
files, tests and clips that show it, read the feature list first. It says No where the answer is no.

## Start here

- [Feature list with evidence](https://github.com/jmaorr/Browsa/blob/main/docs/features.md): every feature, the version it arrived in, where to check it
- [DRM streaming](https://github.com/jmaorr/Browsa/blob/main/docs/drm.md): FairPlay on Browsa's own WebKit build, the check and its result, services played
- [Extensions tested](https://github.com/jmaorr/Browsa/blob/main/docs/web-extensions.md): which Chrome extensions work and which don't
- [What's New](https://browsa.app/whats-new/): each release's features, with a short clip of each
- [Release notes](https://github.com/jmaorr/Browsa/tree/main/docs/release-notes/mac)

## Facts

- [Download](https://browsa.app/download/) and [update feed](https://browsa.app/mac/appcast.xml)
- [Privacy](https://browsa.app/privacy/): no account, analytics or sync
- [Source](https://github.com/jmaorr/Browsa)
